text:
infra-bot: Alert: sustained egress proxy 5xx spike in eu-west for dedicated-pool-23, auto-fallback to soft-slices triggered at 1718523300. Routing error rate ~12% over 5m. Investigating.

Sara: Saw the alert, saw a bunch of tenants spill to soft slices. Any idea which tenant caused the spike?

Ben: Quick check: looks like tenant T-42 had a huge burst of websocket-based embedding requests, CPU and connection churn on the proxy. Metric: `proxy_conn_err_count{pool=dedicated-pool-23}` jumped.

Carla: Ran the query: `sum(rate(proxy_5xx[1m])) by (tenant)` -> T-42 ~= 78 req/s, next is T-19 at 4 req/s. TL;DR: it's T-42.

Dave: Confirmed. Problem is the egress-proxy threadcon currency limit + kernel ephemeral port exhaustion on the proxy hosts. When that hits we start dropping, which triggers our router to reassign to soft slices. Which in turn overloads those slices because they don't have enough egress QPS headroom.

Sara: What's the customer-facing impact? SLOs?

Ben: Some p95 latency spikes for all tenants on that dedicated slice group. Error budget burn modest so far but trending. If this repeats we'll see sustained SLA violations for customers pinned to that pool.

Emma: Proposed immediate mitigation: add a targeted redispatch rule for T-42 to route through a dedicated proxy-pool with higher conn limits in eu-west for 15m while we triage. Then gradually revert.

Dave: +1 to targeted redispatch. We should also increase `proxy_max_conn_per_host` on the affected proxy hosts by 20% and bump the NAT ephemeral port range on the proxies as a follow-up. But raising conn limits has cost/risk.

Carla: Can we do a canary for the redispatch rule? I can push a canary that only affects T-42 on one AZ and monitor `egress_reassign_rate` and `soft_slice_cpu` for 10m.

Sara: Do we have telemetry dashboards for this path? I want top-down: `proxy_5xx`, `egress_reassign_count`, `soft_slice_cpu`, `kvcache_miss_rate` (in case caching changed).

Ben: Dashboards: https://grafana/redwood/d/egress/egress-routing (can monitor those). Suggested alerts: `egress_reassign_rate > 20` for 5m and `soft_slice_cpu > 70%` for 5m.

infra-bot: Suggested runbook step: `redispatch --tenant T-42 --from dedicated-pool-23 --to proxy-highconn-euw --duration 15m --reason "egress conn bloom"` (this is a dry-run until an oncall approves).

Dave: I'll approve. Emma, can you run the dry-run then flip to live if metrics look good?

Emma: Running dry-run now (will post command + output).

Emma: Command: ```
# dry-run
routedb redispatch --tenant T-42 --from=dedicated-pool-23 --to=proxy-highconn-euw --duration=15m --dry-run
```

Emma: Dry-run output: `plan ok; estimated shift 92% of T-42 egress traffic; estimated soft_slice_load +12%`

Carla: That's inline with earlier numbers. Proceed if we're happy with +12% on soft slices.

Sara: What's the cost delta if we route to `proxy-highconn-euw`? That pool is a burst buffer with higher infra cost (gpu slot overhead for headroom).

Ben: Rough calc: 15m of reroute -> ~0.3 GPU-hours across headroom nodes, ~= $1.80 in infra cost. Not material vs SLA risk.

Dave: Also want to set a short-term guardrail: auto-throttle T-42 if egress reassigns > 3 within 30m. Implement via router policy `max-redispatches-per-tenant=3`.

Emma: Live flip now (approving). Running: ```
routedb redispatch --tenant T-42 --from=dedicated-pool-23 --to=proxy-highconn-euw --duration=15m
```

Emma: Result: `redispatch applied id=rd-20260321-001; started`. Monitoring...

Ben: Seeing immediate drop in proxy 5xx from 12% -> 1.4% in the canary AZ. `egress_reassign_rate` also lowered. Initial p95 latency on soft slices stabilized.

Carla: Metric snippets (1m): `proxy_5xx{az=eu-west-1a}` 1.2 -> 0.2, `soft_slice_cpu` +6% but within threshold.

Sara: Great. Let's run the 15m and then roll back. Action items: Emma to monitor and post final status; Dave to file a follow-up to raise NAT ephemeral ports and evaluate permanent routing policy; Ben to draft a short postmortem of root cause (T-42 connection pattern).

Dave: I'll open the issue: INFRA-2347 "egress proxy ephemeral port exhaustion / targeted redispatch playbook" and add recommended kernel tunables and proxy worker scaling.

Emma: Will monitor and ping at +5m and +14m.

infra-bot: Reminder: canary started at 1718523600. Automatic rollback at 1718524500 if `soft_slice_cpu > 85%` or `egress_reassign_rate > 10` for 5m.

Emma: +5m: canary stable. No further 5xx spikes. soft_slice_cpu at +8%.

Sara: Thanks team. After rollback let's schedule a short rehearse of the redispatch path (runbook + operator play) so oncall can do this without real-time coordination. :thumbsup:

Ben: I'll include the playbook steps in the postmortem draft and a small FAQ for SREs.

Dave: Also consider adding a preemptive slope: if one tenant causes >X% of pool egress for >Y min, auto-redispatch to highconn pool instead of soft-slice fallback. Might reduce thundering handoffs.

Carla: Noted. I'll add metrics for that rule to the experiment list.

Emma: Canary ended, redispatch id=rd-20260321-001 rolled back at 1718524500. No regressions. Closing thread unless someone needs follow-up.

Sara: Filing a quick blameless note to T-42 PMs and ops. Good job. :party_parrot:

infra-bot: Thread closed by automation: cleanup tasks scheduled (issue INFRA-2347 created)"
}
